answer: An oasis grain exchange pays agents to verify each delivery lot. A warehouse issues one sealed lot ID after weighing; a random second warehouse checks the seal and mass before payment. The registry links every report to that lot’s provenance thread and uses a mirror comparison to group copied evidence. Fifty fake accounts describing one lot earn one fee. To earn fifty fees, an attacker must move and store fifty real lots or forge seals while risking deposits and inspection costs. Colluding warehouses could certify phantom grain, so buyers audit inventory at surprise times and permit disputes.
